correctness.rationale: The reduced plane-cubic discriminant has degree 12, so a basepoint-free quadratic parametrization yields a discriminant of binary degree 24. Over the stated nodal locus the unique nodes identify the root cover with the one-marked incidence. Evaluation at one or two distinct base points is surjective, and a node at a prescribed point gives three independent linear conditions on a cubic; the corresponding single and ordered-pair incidence spaces are open subsets of irreducible vector bundles after restriction to U. For the local collision at [1:0] with node x, the nondegenerate fiber Hessian gives the critical-value germ ε+κτ² with κ≠0. To justify the genericity away from that parameter under the imposed constraints, use w=s/t on its complement: H freely varies the cubic Fw²+2Gw+H at fixed w, and a variation of G vanishing at x, balanced by H, independently varies its parameter derivative at any other candidate node y≠x. The excluded node y=x cannot occur there when H(x)≠0. Thus a second tangency has four independent conditions over the three-dimensional space of (parameter,node), and non-unique or nonordinary nodes are avoided by the codimension-two estimate and free cubic evaluation. This supplies a lone transposition by a small loop; two-transitivity then gives S₂₄, and the rational coefficient-field group contains it. The class pairings are e²=0, e·h=3, h²=2 and divisibility 3 for both e and 3h−e in the cited very general lattice. Over the dense open where F,G,H have no common projective zero, projection to the plane is a relative finite flat double cover; its relative involution identifies the marked-fiber covers by transporting π to π∘ι. This supplies the family-level conclusion, not just equality of fiber counts one surface at a time. The frozen verification and finite SymPy diagnostic were inspected; the script was not executed.

originality.rationale: The central symmetric-group claim follows from the established characteristic-zero sectional monodromy theorem, not just the general Harris proof technique or an analogy with Weierstrass K3s. In the full (2,3) triple family restrict F,G,H to be frames of a fixed general projective plane Λ in the space of cubics. The section C=Λ∩Δ is geometrically integral by Bertini and has degree 12. Its quadratic Veronese image is a nondegenerate integral curve of degree 24 in P⁵ (no conic contains C). Its generic hyperplane sections are conic sections of C and have S₂₄ monodromy by Kadets, Proposition 1.1. The frames with their fixed standard quadratic parametrization range over all smooth conics in Λ; the frame-to-conic map has geometrically connected fibers, the inverse image in GL₃ of the conic stabilizer PGL₂ in PGL₃. Therefore extension to the frame function field does not shrink the Galois group. Restricting to the open of smooth total surfaces and transverse nodal sections also does not change it, and a subfamily with S₂₄ forces S₂₄ in the full family. The stated lattice and exchanged pencils are prior, their indices follow from the lattice pairings, and the relative involution gives the same root cover for the companion. This is demonstrable implication by prior theorems, without asserting priority between same-day catalogue entries.
residual_risks: No claim is made about the first explicit publication of this exact coefficient formulation or a deformation comparison with the triquadratic family. Neither question affects the demonstrated prior implication.

value.rationale: The singular-fiber permutation group is a natural invariant, and the direct proof is a useful illustration. As a claimed new exact invariant it does not fill an independent mathematical gap: standard Veronese sectional monodromy forces it, and the rest is the known rank-two geometry and its immediate index and transport consequences. No narrower independently useful new claim is established in the frozen finding.
